title: Coefficient quotient of a vector-space-valued functor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S$ a small category and $F:S\to\operatorname{Mod}_k$ a functor to $k$-vector spaces. Use tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $T_V=\operatorname{Hom}_k(F(V),k)\otimes_k F(V)$ and $T=\bigoplus_{V\in S}T_V$, with its canonical linear inclusions $j_V$. Define $N\subseteq T$ as the linear span of all $j_W(\psi\otimes F(f)v)-j_V((\psi\circ F(f))\otimes v)$ for $f:V\to W$, $v\in F(V)$ and $\psi\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(F(W),k)$. The coefficient quotient is $B(F)=T/N$, with $c_V(\phi,v)$ the quotient image of $j_V(\phi\otimes v)$. Given an equivalence $e:S\simeq\mathcal A$ with counit $a_V:e(e^{-1}V)\simeq V$ and $G:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Mod}_k$, define $c_V^e(\phi,v)=c_{e^{-1}V}(\phi\circ G(a_V),G(a_V^{-1})v)$ in $B(G\circ e)$. All sums lie in a fixed containing universe. No finite dimension or exactness is needed for this quotient definition.
